notable_absence.finding: This overview page states no role, credential-type, edition, or version gating at all for the Analytics Service itself - access is deferred entirely to the deployment mechanism (cluster creation / scale-database) and to the sub-feature pages (analytics-links.md, analytics-workbench.md, this batch) that DO name a role gate. No storage-engine mention either, consistent with storage engines being a Data Service/bucket-level concept the Analytics Service inherits indirectly via its Data Service dependency, not something it exposes directly.

cross_component_finding: The 'up to 8 datasets' ceiling is the first Analytics-specific numeric constraint found in this batch, parallel in kind (though smaller) to data-service.json's 30-bucket/1000-scope/1000-collection ceilings.
cross_product_finding: PRIMARY FINDING for this batch's second hypothesis question (does the Analytics Service have its own access-control model?): on this page, no - Analytics Service availability is gated purely by service deployment (must be added to the cluster), the same mechanism already established for Query/Index/Search Service dependency chains, not by any Analytics-specific role or credential concept. The actual access-control answer is confirmed on the sub-pages: analytics-links.json and analytics-workbench.json (this batch) both show the Analytics Workbench gated by the pre-existing capella-role:* project-role catalog (Project Owner / Data Writer) - the exact same catalog used for bucket administration (data-service.json) and document access (manage-documents.json). The Analytics Service reuses Capella's one project-role catalog rather than defining its own.
